name: Earth Systems (Min)

rules.name: Foundational Courses
rules.notes: Students may not double count Earthsys 115.

rules.name: Electives
rules.desc:
A minimum of 3 units must be taken in each of the following categories: 1) Earth Systems Science/Engineering; 2) Environmental Justice; 3) Applied Problem Solving; and 4) Skills.
Courses appearing in multiple categories may not be re-used.

rules.name: Category 1: Earth Systems Science/ Engineering
rules.notes: Students may apply up to 16 units of Earthsys 323: Stanford at Sea across Categories 1, 3, and 4.

rules.name: Category 3: Applied Problem Solving
rules.notes: Students may apply up to 16 units of Earthsys 323: Stanford at Sea across Categories 1, 3, and 4.

rules.name: Category 4: Skills
rules.notes: Students may apply up to 16 units of Earthsys 323: Stanford at Sea across Categories 1, 3, and 4.

blocks.name: Environmental Justice, Ethics, and Human Rights Subplan

rules.name: Gateway
rules.desc: Students must complete a minimum of 24 units of Environmental Justice-related coursework.

rules.name: Reflection
rules.desc: Students will write a formal reflection to integrate and synthesize learning from coursework in the Environmental Justice Minor, including community-engaged learning experiences and relevant co-curricular learning achieved through involvement with student or community organizations.

rules.name: Cardinal Course - Community Engaged Learning
rules.desc:
A minimum of 12 units must be earned by completing coursework with a community-engaged learning component. These units must be earned in courses designated as Cardinal Courses by the Haas Center; alternatively, a student may petition for one non-Cardinal Course that includes a community-engaged component to count toward this requirement.
These courses will require students to synthesize multiple sources of knowledge to understand EJ problems, develop solutions, and build understanding and gain experience in engaging ethically with community members and organizations across power imbalances (see Principles of Ethical and Effective Service).
Students will be eligible for the Cardinal Service Notation by fulfilling requirements for the Minor in Earth Systems, Environmental Justice subplan.
rules.notes: Cardinal Courses may be doubled counted across requirements.

gpa: In accordance with University policy, students must maintain a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0.
grading: All courses counted toward the minor must be taken for a letter grade, except when a letter grade option is not available, and must be passed with a grade of at least D-.
transferPolicy: Courses may be fulfilled through approved AP credit, Stanford placement tests, or transfer credit, where applicable. Students can submit a petition for such credit to be counted.
reviewNotes: In the Sustainability subplan you take the five foundational courses and at least 3 units in each of the four elective categories, at least 28 units in all, with no course used twice and at most 16 units of EARTHSYS 323 counted. In the Environmental Justice subplan you take EARTHSYS 194, one course each in movements, ethical frameworks and practice, EARTHSYS 134, and 12 units of Cardinal Courses, which may also count for the other requirements, for at least 24 units. Every course must be letter graded when that option exists and passed with a D- or better. You check by hand a petitioned non-Cardinal community-engaged course and the 2.0 GPA.
